title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν} (cote 147). Here M_{g,I} is the moduli stack of curves of genus g with marked points indexed by the finite set I. For a stable ('MD') graph G, M_G is the corresponding boundary stratum of the Deligne–Mumford compactification. π1 M_G is its fundamental groupoid, which factors as a product over the vertices of G. Sπ1 M_G is the fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of the stratum. It is an extension of π1 M_G by Z^{edges}, the edges giving the loops around the boundary divisors.

The previous page set a programme. It asks for all these groupoids, with two kinds of maps between them:
- generalisation morphisms Sπ1 M_G → Sπ1 M_{G'}, attached to graph contractions G → G';
- normalisation morphisms, attached to monomorphisms I' ↪ I (eq. (148)).
The aim was a description by generators and relations.

This page opens §12, 'Relation between generalisation morphisms and normalisation (?) morphisms'. Before any explicit computation, Grothendieck wants to study how the two kinds of morphism interact. He notes as trivial that, for graph morphisms, both are compatible with the projections Sπ1 M_G → π1 M_G. For a strict inclusion I' ⊂ I he wants to see 'the effect at infinity' of the morphisms (148).

Setup:
- G_{g,I} is the reduced graph: a single vertex of genus g with the legs I. It corresponds to the open stack M_{g,I}.
- G is any stable graph of modular type (g, ν = card I).
- A generalisation morphism G → G_{g,I} (149) amounts to the contraction of all edges of G together with a bijection I(G) ≅ I between the legs of G and I.
- From this comes a diagram of multiplicités (stacks) (150):
  - M*_{G,G_{g,I}}, the deleted tubular neighbourhood of M_G inside M_{g,I}, maps to M_{g,I};
  - it is also equivalent (or retracts) to (M_{G,G_{g,I}}, Γ^!_G), a punctured normal-bundle-type object over the stratum;
  - this object is in turn linked to (M_G, Γ^!_G).

Taking π1 of this diagram gives the generalisation map Sπ1 M_G → π1 M_{g,I}, which is a 'tangential base point' type map. The page stops here.

The whole page is struck through by a long diagonal line. The next sheet is §11, a 'digression' on unfolding normal crossings divisors, and it reuses the equation number (149). This suggests §12 was abandoned in this form and redone after the general local study of normal crossings.
errors: No mathematical error visible. The page is cancelled (diagonal strike-through), and the equation numbers (149) and (150) clash with the following §11, which also uses (149). This page is therefore a discarded first draft of §12.

The diagram (150) is only partially legible. The exact meaning of Γ^!_G (probably the local system or normal data of the branches of the boundary divisor along the stratum) is not defined on this page.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum, Sπ1 M_G, as an extension of π1 M_G by Z^{edges}, with a 'generalisation' map to π1 M_{g,I}.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / fundamental groupoid at infinity of M_{g,n}; local monodromy at boundary strata (Dehn twists around separating and non-separating curves)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara–Nakamura; Nakamura; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Boggi
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3: the 'Teichmüller tower', the 'jeu de Lego' and the structure at infinity in rough form

ideas.what: Studying compatibility between generalisation (graph contraction) morphisms and normalisation/forgetful morphisms attached to I' ⊂ I, at the level of fundamental groupoids at infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of clutching and forgetful maps (Knudsen) on fundamental groupoids; operadic/modular-operad structure of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (algebro-geometric compatibilities); Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps (groupoid level); Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads)
ideas.where_published: Hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (the tower in its dependence on ν via operations), not in this explicit form

ideas.what: Diagram (150): deleted tubular neighbourhood of a stratum, its retraction onto the punctured normal data over M_G, and its map to M_{g,I}.
ideas.modern_name: Punctured tubular neighbourhood / deformation to the normal cone of a normal crossings stratum (Kato–Nakayama log topology)

missed.claim: Grothendieck planned a systematic study of how forgetful/normalisation morphisms (I' ⊂ I) act 'at infinity' on the extensions Sπ1 M_G, in compatibility with graph-contraction morphisms, as a step towards a generators-and-relations presentation of the whole Teichmüller tower of groupoids. This draft is abandoned and redone after a general digression on normal crossings divisors. The content is largely covered by later work (Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Boggi), so novelty is limited.
missed.quote: j'ai envie, pour une inclusion stricte I' ⊂ I, d'examiner "l'effet à l'infini" des morphismes de [normalisation] (148)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents an early stack-theoretic, groupoid-level formulation of the boundary structure of M_{g,n} that predates the 'Lego' and tangential base point literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A crossed-out start of a section; the ideas (fundamental groupoid at infinity, compatibility of clutching and forgetful maps) are known and partly sketched in the Esquisse. Of historical interest only.
transcription_corrections: Title: probably 'Relation entre [-les-] morphismes de généralisation et morphismes de normalisation' (not 'multiplication'); the second line of the title is underlined.
'des morphismes de Grothendieck-Teichmüller [?] (148)' is surely wrong: the word refers back to (148), i.e. the morphismes de normalisation (possibly 'd'oubli') of the previous page.
'd'où un [-diag-] gramme de multiplication' should read 'd'où un diagramme de multiplicités'.
'Soit G un graphe ... [?]' is probably 'Soit G un graphe MD-pointé'.
The whole page is struck through by a long diagonal line (cancelled draft). The page number at bottom left is 104.
